executiveSummary: Surveillance data from ECDC (Weeks 16-20, April-May 2026) and PAHO (October 2025-May 2026) reveal multiple concurrent public health threats across the Americas and Europe. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) continues to circulate in the Americas region with ongoing animal-human interface risk, representing the highest-priority biosafety concern as a BSL-3 select agent. Additional significant threats include Mpox in the Americas, Yellow Fever, Dengue, and a resurgent Pertussis wave, alongside the start of the Southern Hemisphere influenza season. Measles re-emergence and Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome round out a complex multi-pathogen threat landscape requiring coordinated regional response.
bottomLine: Avian Influenza A(H5N1) at the animal-human interface remains the critical biosecurity priority, compounded by simultaneous resurgence of vaccine-preventable diseases and vector-borne threats across the Americas and Europe.

threats.name: Avian Influenza A(H5N1)
signals: Multiple PAHO epidemiological updates issued November 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained circulation
Ongoing animal-human interface exposure events in the Americas
BSL-3 select agent with pandemic potential requiring heightened surveillance
Dual alerts issued 5 months apart suggesting no containment achieved
threats.action: Activate enhanced surveillance at animal-human interface; ensure healthcare worker PPE and antiviral stockpiles; sequence all human-proximate isolates; coordinate with USDA/FAO on poultry outbreak mapping

threats.name: Mpox
signals: PAHO epidemiological update issued April 23, 2026 indicating active transmission
Sustained circulation in the Americas following global clade Ib concerns
BSL-3 select agent requiring contact tracing and isolation protocols
Ongoing update cycle suggests unresolved transmission chains
threats.action: Strengthen case detection and contact tracing; promote vaccine access in high-risk populations; ensure BSL-3 laboratory diagnostic capacity; coordinate with ECDC on travel-linked cases

threats.name: Dengue
signals: PAHO epidemiological update February 18, 2026 indicating high case burden
Historically record-breaking dengue seasons in the Americas in recent years
Vector (Aedes aegypti) range expansion linked to climate patterns
Risk of severe dengue and healthcare system strain in endemic countries
threats.action: Intensify vector control programs; ensure clinical case management capacity; monitor serotype shifts that may increase severe disease risk; issue travel health advisories

threats.name: Seasonal Influenza (Southern Hemisphere Season Start)
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued April 27, 2026 marking start of Southern Hemisphere season
Simultaneous circulation of RSV and influenza flagged in January 2026 alert
Co-circulation with other respiratory pathogens increases healthcare burden
Prior December 2025 alert signaled transition between hemispheric seasons
threats.action: Promote Southern Hemisphere seasonal influenza vaccination; strengthen syndromic surveillance; prepare hospital surge capacity; monitor for novel reassortant strains given concurrent H5N1 circulation

threats.name: Pertussis (Whooping Cough)
signals: Two separate PAHO alerts issued December 2025 and March 2026 indicating sustained resurgence
Multi-month persistence suggests vaccination gaps or waning immunity driving transmission
Infant and immunocompromised populations at high risk of severe outcomes
Resurgence pattern consistent with global pertussis wave observed in multiple regions
threats.action: Audit vaccination coverage and close immunization gaps; promote Tdap boosters in adolescents, adults, and pregnant women; enhance diagnostic capacity; investigate potential macrolide resistance

threats.name: Yellow Fever
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued March 13, 2026 indicating active risk
Epizootics in non-human primates serve as early warning of human spillover risk
Unvaccinated populations in endemic and buffer zones remain vulnerable
Alert issued during period of active PAHO multi-pathogen monitoring
threats.action: Ensure vaccination coverage in at-risk populations and travelers; conduct emergency vaccination campaigns in outbreak zones; strengthen primate mortality surveillance as early warning system; enforce vaccination requirements at borders

threats.name: Measles
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued February 3, 2026 indicating re-emergence risk
Vaccination coverage gaps identified in the post-COVID period enabling resurgence
Risk of importation-driven outbreaks in under-vaccinated communities
Americas region had achieved measles elimination status now under threat
threats.action: Conduct vaccination coverage assessments; implement targeted catch-up campaigns in under-vaccinated communities; strengthen port-of-entry surveillance; ensure outbreak response capacity within 48 hours of case detection

threats.name: Hantavirus Pulmonary Syndrome
signals: PAHO epidemiological alert issued December 19, 2025 indicating active cases
High case fatality rate (30-40%) makes even small outbreaks significant
Rodent population dynamics and climate variability drive exposure risk
Alert timing in Southern Hemisphere summer aligns with peak transmission season
threats.action: Issue public health advisories on rodent avoidance; strengthen rural healthcare worker training for early recognition; ensure ribavirin availability where applicable; monitor rodent reservoir populations in endemic areas

selectAgentSummary: Two BSL-3 select agents are actively circulating in the Americas region. Avian Influenza A(H5N1) has triggered two separate PAHO epidemiological updates (November 2025 and March 2026), indicating sustained animal reservoir activity with human spillover risk; this pathogen is classified as a USDA/CDC overlap select agent with pandemic potential. Monkeypox virus (MPXV) has triggered a PAHO update in April 2026, with ongoing transmission requiring BSL-3 laboratory handling and specialized public health response. Both pathogens require enhanced biosafety protocols, specialized laboratory infrastructure, and coordinated international response frameworks beyond standard public health measures.
amrSignals: Pertussis resurgence over multiple months may indicate macrolide antibiotic resistance in Bordetella pertussis strains warranting molecular surveillance
GLP-1 receptor agonist medication misuse alert (PAHO February 2026) suggests counterfeit/substandard pharmaceutical supply chains that may parallel antimicrobial resistance drivers
Extended influenza season activity raises concern for antiviral (oseltamivir) resistance emergence particularly in H5N1 strains under treatment pressure
emergingPatterns: Simultaneous multi-pathogen resurgence across Americas suggests systemic post-pandemic vaccination coverage gaps enabling vaccine-preventable disease rebounds (Measles, Pertussis)
Dual H5N1 alerts five months apart without resolution indicates endemic establishment in animal reservoirs across the Americas rather than isolated outbreaks

Co-circulation of multiple respiratory pathogens (Influenza A, Influenza B, RSV, potential H5N1) creates diagnostic confusion risk and healthcare surge vulnerability heading into Southern Hemisphere winter 2026
Vector-borne disease pressure (Dengue, Chikungunya, Yellow Fever) appearing simultaneously suggests Aedes and other vector populations are broadly expanding, likely climate-driven
ECDC issuing five consecutive weekly threat reports (Weeks 16-20) indicates sustained elevated multi-threat monitoring posture in Europe concurrent with Americas alerts

Methanol poisoning alert (October 2025) and GLP-1 misuse alert (February 2026) reflect emerging non-infectious public health threats from counterfeit/substandard products requiring integrated surveillance systems
